description: A chief legal officer must approve the company's annual-meeting proxy statement and finalize its related-party disclosure, director-election instructions, and executive-compensation response, with input from securities, corporate-governance, and executive-compensation specialists.

shared_context.S1: The company's annual shareholder meeting is scheduled for six weeks from today, and the proxy statement is in final legal review.
shared_context.S2: The board has approved the current director slate and executive-compensation proposal.
shared_context.S3: Elena Brooks gives the final legal approval for the proxy statement and its accompanying filing package.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's routine proxy sign-off, Elena asks securities counsel, the corporate secretary, and executive-compensation counsel to report any checklist item that must be added or changed before approval.

PF1.text: Martin reconciled a late finance ledger this week and confirmed that a company executive's spouse-owned consulting entity received exactly $275,000 during the fiscal year. The transaction is a related-person transaction requiring disclosure of the exact amount and relationship in the proxy, plus an audit-committee-review statement; Martin has not yet updated the disclosure markup.

PF2.text: During a fresh review of the governing bylaws, Nadia confirmed that the director-election section must state that shareholders may vote for no more than three nominees, rather than using the draft's generic voting instruction. She found this after the governance checklist was circulated and has not revised the proxy draft.

PF3.text: Theo received the finalized prior-year say-on-pay tabulation after the proxy draft was prepared: 68% of votes supported the proposal. The company's compensation policy treats support below exactly 70% as requiring an enhanced proxy rationale and a written shareholder-engagement summary; Theo has not added those materials yet.

acceptance_conditions: The proxy must disclose the related-person transaction for exactly $275,000.
The proxy must include a statement that the transaction was reviewed by the audit committee.
The director-election instructions must state that shareholders may vote for no more than three nominees.
The proxy must include an enhanced rationale for the executive-compensation proposal.
The proxy must include a written shareholder-engagement summary.
The final package must include a related-person disclosure update commitment targeting Martin Shaw.
The securities finding must be cited as justification for the related-person disclosure.

content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Martin Shaw' and c['type'] in ['conditional_approval', 'addition_required', 'markup_revision', 'disclosure_update', 'update'] and '$275,000' in c['detail'] and 'audit-committee-review' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The late ledger reconciliation changes the proxy from no specified related-person disclosure to disclosure of exactly $275,000, an audit-committee-review statement, and an update commitment targeting Martin Shaw.
The bylaw review changes the director-election instruction from a generic voting direction to an exact limit of no more than three nominees.
The finalized 68% vote result crosses the policy's exact 70% threshold and changes the compensation section to require both an enhanced rationale and a written shareholder-engagement summary.
